item.name: Favorite
item.description: The calling user's personal favorites list (`services/favorite/`).

description.content:
Adds an item to the calling user's favorites. Favoriting an item that is
already favorited succeeds and changes nothing (`already_favorited:
true`). Fails with 422 when the user already holds 500 favorites —
nothing is inserted and no existing favorite is evicted. Answers 404
when the item does not exist in the catalog.

response.name: The item is now in the caller's favorites.

Returns everything the calling user has favorited, most recently
favorited first. An item discontinued in the catalog after it was
favorited is still listed, with `available: false` — the availability
flag is read live from the catalog, not copied at favorite-time.

An empty list is a normal response: `favorites` is `[]`, never `null`.

Taking no sort or filter parameters is deliberate for this pass;
`created_at` is retained so a later pass can add them without a
migration.

description.content:
Removes the item from the calling user's favorites.

Answers 404 both when the item was never favorited and when the row
belongs to another user — the two are deliberately indistinguishable, so
this endpoint cannot be used to enumerate other users' favorites. A path
segment that is not a positive integer takes the same 404.
(Required) The catalog item's id.

response.name: The item is no longer in the caller's favorites.

description.content:
sandbox-svc — the favorite-items feature (FEAT-001), the CSV export
(FEAT-003), and the favorites summary (FEAT-005).

Five routes: favorite an item, list your favorites, un-favorite one,
summarize your favorites, and export them as a CSV download. Every route
acts on the calling user's own rows only; the user is taken from the access
token, never from the request, so no route accepts a user id.

Paths, methods and tags for the four JSON routes are emitted by
nexcommon's own generator (`GenerateSwaggerDocs`, served at
`/swagger/swagger.yaml`), so they cannot drift from the routes the service
registers. `GET /v1/favorites/export` is the exception: it is registered
directly on the mux router, because the response is a file with its own
headers rather than the JSON envelope, so the generator cannot see it and
this document is its only contract. The response side of every route — the
`{success, header, payload}` envelope, the per-status coverage, the
business error codes, and examples taken from the real DTOs — is authored
here for the same reason.
